sources.rank_basis: tier B, rated by class: a company's engineering blog (percona.com/blog, post by Robert Bernier dated April 13, 2022). Rule 1 does not apply (no evidence in the input that the author originated the concept); rule 2 does not apply (Percona is not the PostgreSQL project, and the claims are about PostgreSQL); rule 3 does not apply (not a mailing-list post). The rank covers the article body only, lines 1-1035 of the saved page; lines 1036 onward are reader comments and count as Rank 6 (stage1 note).
tier A: reader comments (#comments). Covers lines 1036 onward of the saved page, including the post author's own replies.

claim_checks.claim: PostgreSQL forces a shutdown to protect the data when the number of unique transaction IDs reaches its maximum, and Percona's post gives queries that report how close each database is
claim_checks.page_says: Postgres will force a shutdown in order to protect the data. ... Here is a set of queries that will help you determine if wraparound is a risk
claim_checks.note: Summary judged at role 5, the strictest of the sections it summarizes (1, 2, 5). Both parts are in the article body (lines 396 and 451-461); the database query reports age per database and as a percentage of the maximum.

claim_checks.claim: PostgreSQL tracks transactions with unique IDs, and the count approaches an upper limit that can be registered
claim_checks.page_says: PostgreSQL tracks transactions using unique IDs. Every so often, that number approaches the upper limit that can be registered.
claim_checks.note: Line 396. The claim states no frequency, so leaving out the page's 'every so often' does not make it stronger.

claim_checks.claim: The post's database-level query reports `age(datfrozenxid)` per database, and a column it names `% WRAPAROUND RISK`
claim_checks.page_says: -- Database query for transaction age per database ... age(datfrozenxid), (age(datfrozenxid)::numeric / 1000000000 * 100)::numeric(4, 2) AS "% WRAPAROUND RISK" FROM pg_database

claim_checks.claim: Its table-level query takes the greater of a table's `relfrozenxid` age and its TOAST table's
claim_checks.page_says: greatest(age(c.relfrozenxid), age(t.relfrozenxid)) AS "TXID age", ... LEFT JOIN pg_class t ON c.reltoastrelid = t.oid
claim_checks.note: Lines 501-510. The join on reltoastrelid makes t the table's TOAST relation, so the greatest() is over the table's age and its TOAST table's age.

claim_checks.claim: 200 million transactions is the default threshold used by `autovacuum_freeze_max_age`
claim_checks.page_says: For example, 200 million transactions is the default threshold used by autovacuum_freeze_max_age.

claim_checks.claim: VACUUM cannot operate on a TOAST table alone, so to vacuum a TOAST table you vacuum the table it belongs to
claim_checks.page_says: not found in the article body (lines 1-1035); searched: toast, relation, belongs, 'vacuum the table'
claim_checks.note: The article body mentions TOAST only inside its queries (reltoastrelid joins). The statement appears only at line 1112, in the post author's reply inside the reader comments (Rank 6 from line 1036 on): 'vacuum cannot operate on TOAST tables alone'. Another reader in the same thread contradicts it ('I can run a manual vacuum on the TOAST table', line 1130; and line 1084). So the claim takes Rank 6 material, cites it under the Rank 4 label, and states one side of an unsettled disagreement as fact in role 3.

claim_checks.claim: The post's sample log message for a database close to shutdown carries the hint "To avoid a database shutdown, execute a database-wide VACUUM in "mydb"."
claim_checks.page_says: Here is an example error message that you can find in the Postgres logs when threatened by shutdown due to wraparound: ... HINT: To avoid a database shutdown, execute a database-wide VACUUM in "mydb".
claim_checks.note: Lines 426-432. Grounded, but the section is a quoted sample rather than a run with inputs and outputs (see structure violation).

claim_checks.claim: 2 billion transactions is the upper limit that PostgreSQL permits before forcing a shutdown
claim_checks.page_says: 2 billion transactions, or 231, is the upper limit that PostgreSQL permits before forcing a shutdown.
claim_checks.note: Line 402 ('231' is 2 to the power 31 with the superscript lost in the saved text).

claim_checks.claim: One reader in a wraparound situation listed the oldest tables and found they were all TOAST tables, and reported no problem vacuuming a TOAST table directly
claim_checks.page_says: found myself facing the wraparound situation and grabbed a list of oldest tables ... they were all TOAST tables. ... there didn’t seem to be any problem manually vacuuming the TOAST directly
claim_checks.note: Line 1084, a Rank 6 reader comment cited in role 6, which allows any rank. The claim keeps it as one reader's report. Checked because it cites a Rank 6 source. It conflicts with the claim in section 3 item 2, and the doc does not say so.

conflicts.topic: Whether VACUUM can process a TOAST table on its own
conflicts.winner: none: both sides are Rank 6 reader comments (the author's reply at line 1112 vs reader Eddie at lines 1084 and 1130); no Rank 1 source is cached to settle it
conflicts.loser: the author's comment 'vacuum cannot operate on TOAST tables alone' (Rank 6), cited as [^percona] at Rank 4

criteria_checks.criterion: Sections 2 and 5 must name the query column that reports wraparound risk.
criteria_checks.evidence: Section 2 (role 2) names `% WRAPAROUND RISK` (line 23). Section 5 (role 5) does not name it: its line 35 says only 'The risk columns are defined in §2.' Unlike the second criterion, this one has no 'together', so each section must name the column.

criteria_checks.criterion: Sections 3 and 5 together must give both the 200 million default threshold and the 2 billion upper limit.
criteria_checks.evidence: Section 3 (role 3) line 27 gives 200 million for autovacuum_freeze_max_age; section 5 (role 5) line 34 gives the 2 billion limit. Both are grounded (C5, C8).

violations.evidence: C6: the claim that VACUUM cannot operate on a TOAST table alone is not in the cited article body. It appears only in the author's reply among the reader comments (line 1112, Rank 6).

C6 relies only on text below the '=== READER COMMENTS BELOW (Rank 6: unvetted) ===' boundary (line 1036) but cites it as [^percona] at Rank 4. Role 3 allows only ranks 1-4, so a Rank 6 comment is supporting a mechanism claim.

Two same-rank (Rank 6) comments disagree on whether a TOAST table can be vacuumed directly: the author's reply (line 1112) says no, and a reader (lines 1084, 1130) says he did it. The doc states the 'no' side as fact in role 3 and the other side in section 6 with no '⚖️ open conflict' mark, and no Rank 1 source settles it.
CAL-02 requires sections 2 and 5 to name the wraparound-risk query column. Section 5 only points to section 2 ('The risk columns are defined in §2.').
The section quotes one sample log line from the post. It shows no run: no input (a database's age(datfrozenxid)) and no query output.

The reference section gives one value and a pointer to section 2 instead of the exact values it should list (column names, the 10 million warning and 1 million read-only points the post gives at lines 404-406).
A single reader anecdote. It has no trade-off or decision table, and it does not say that it contradicts section 3 item 2.

patch_instructions.action: Delete item 2 ('VACUUM cannot operate on a TOAST table alone, so to vacuum a TOAST table you vacuum the table it belongs to ✅[^percona]'). The article body of [^percona] does not say it; only the author's reply in the comments does (line 1112, Rank 6).

Replace the bullet with a '⚖️ open conflict' entry giving each side its own source and rank: (a) the post author, replying in the comments, says VACUUM cannot operate on TOAST tables alone and you must vacuum the owning table [^percona-comments], Rank 6; (b) a reader reports that the oldest tables in his wraparound situation were all TOAST tables, that manually vacuuming a TOAST table directly worked and ran faster, and that autovacuum processes TOAST tables separately [^percona-comments], Rank 6. State that no Rank 1 source in the input settles it. To settle it, fetch and cite the PostgreSQL VACUUM documentation; the post links routine-vacuuming.html, but that page is not cached.

Replace 'The risk columns are defined in §2.' with a bullet that names the column, for example: '`% WRAPAROUND RISK`: the column that the post's database-level and table-level queries use to report wraparound risk ✅[^percona]' (lines 459 and 505). Optionally add the post's 10 million warning point and 1 million read-only point ✅[^percona] (lines 404-406).

Turn the section into a run with input and output: show the post's database-level query, an example row with age(datfrozenxid) and the resulting `% WRAPAROUND RISK`, and the log lines that come with it. Back any output you did not take from the post with a probe. The post's own sample is not consistent: its comment says 'fewer than 10 million transactions remain' while its WARNING says 177009986 transactions (lines 430-431). Either do not present the sample as a 10-million-point case, or record the mismatch in section 6.

Optionally add a pitfall grounded in [^percona]: the post's `% WRAPAROUND RISK` divides age by 1,000,000,000 (lines 459 and 505) while the post gives 2 billion as the shutdown limit (line 402), so 100% in that column marks 1 billion transactions, half the stated limit.
